title: PRD: Minimal Hosted Endpoint Behavior + Operational Exit Criteria
creator: Ravi Kumar
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines a compact, operationally-safe minimal behavioral contract for Redwood hosted inference endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). The goal is to publish a lightweight, well-scoped surface that is easy to adopt (low cognitive overhead for integrators) while providing explicit operational exit criteria and eval-gated acceptance so launch can be run with a narrow blast radius.

Why this exists:
- Multiple product docs and teams requested a single minimal contract for early adopters and lighthouse customers that reduces feature combinations and isolates production risk.
- We need a formal set of acceptance gates (quality + reliability + cost) so that engineering and ops can make go/no-go decisions consistently.

Goals (measurable):
1) Behavioral minimalism: define the smallest consistent contract for request/response semantics across generation, chat, embeddings, and rerank.
2) Eval gating: ability to run prompt-based quality checks during canary slices and block rollout on regression thresholds.
3) Operational exit criteria: concrete SLOs, monitoring dashboards, and rollback triggers documented for on-call.
4) Developer ergonomics: simple SDK surface for the minimal contract and clear migration notes to the full hosted surface.

In-scope (minimum viable):
- API surface: single /v1/infer endpoint with a typed mode parameter: {"mode":"chat|generate|embed|rerank"}. Mode-specific parameters minimal and documented.
- Determinism guidance for reproducible evals: default deterministic=false, seed optional. Document expected nondeterminism and token-level variance bands.
- Response envelopes: status, primary output, tokens_used, model_version, model_variant, latency_ms.
- Eval hooks: ability to attach an eval_id and receive per-request eval metadata back for offline quality scoring.
- Canary rollout support: traffic slice header X-Redwood-Slice for traffic shaping.
- Fallthrough behavior: explicit fallback map (model_variants) for low-capacity scenarios; documented degrade modes (latency-first, cost-first, quality-first).

Out-of-scope (for this ticket):
- Multi-message session state beyond ephemeral KV prefix caching (full chat history orchestration lives in a follow-up).
- Advanced function/tool calling and rich function schemas.
- Fine-grained per-token billing changes and long-term cost experiments.

Behavioral requirements (per mode):
- Chat: accepts messages array with role/contents; returns messages array with top-level content and optional metadata. Guarantees single-best candidate returned for minimal surface (no n-best).
- Generate (completions): accepts prompt string and max_tokens; returns text, stop_reason. No streaming in MVP.
- Embeddings: accepts list of inputs (max batch 16); returns vector per input. Embedding dimensionality must be included in metadata.
- Rerank: accepts query and candidate list up to 32; returns ranking with scores normalized 0..1 and top_k selection optional.

Acceptance criteria (gated):
Quality gates (eval-driven):
- For each mode, a suite of 100 representative prompts (from existing eval bank) must show no more than: chat - 3% regression in task-level correctness; generate - 5% regression in BLEU/ROUGE style metric where applicable; embeddings - cosine similarity drop <= 2% vs baseline; rerank - NDCG@10 drop <= 1.5%.
- Regression measurement tooling integrated with CI so that PRs exposing >threshold regressions are flagged.

Reliability gates:
- P99 latency at 512-token distribution: chat <= 420ms for tier-1 model_variants, generate <= 300ms, embed <= 120ms, rerank <= 240ms.
- Error rate (5xx) <= 0.2% averaged over 24h during canary slice.
- Circuit-breaker thresholds: if error rate >1% for 30m or P95 latency deteriorates by >2x vs baseline for 15m, automatic rollback to previous model_variant.

Cost & capacity gates:
- Unit cost estimate within 20% of projected runbook numbers for a standard 50 qps profile.
- Autoscaling: can allocate reserved capacity within 10 minutes per our Dedicated contracts; if not met, restrict routed traffic to previous lane.

Operational exit criteria (what triggers an abort/rollback):
- Quality regression exceeded on live eval probes for 3 consecutive 10-minute windows.
- Sustained error rate >0.5% for 60 minutes with no mitigating explanation from infra.
- Manual exec escalation from trust & safety or customer success for high-severity customer reports.

Telemetry & dashboards required before canary:
- Per-mode latency histogram, token counts, request size distribution, model_variant mix.
- Eval probe dashboard showing probe-level pass/fail and rolling trend.
- Cost-per-token and per-request cost estimate with 24h reconciliation against billing.
- Error taxonomy (client errors, backend model errors, infra errors) with top-5 root causes.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Internal dogfood run (internal tenants only) - 48h smoke and engagement tests.
2) 1% external traffic canary for 48h with eval hooks active.
3) 10% external slice for 72h and full monitoring.
4) 100% cutover after 7 days of stable metrics.
Each phase must pass acceptance criteria and have a documented cutover checklist and rollback playbook.

Developer-facing docs & SDKs:
- Quickstart examples for each mode (curl + JS + Python) with minimal examples and explicit migration notes.
- Behavioral FAQ listing known nondeterminism patterns and recommended eval prompt designs.

Security & compliance:
- All requests must pass tenant auth tokens; audit logs kept for all requests during canary.
- Security review required (see field security_review_required). KMS integration described in companion doc.

Operational runbooks (to be attached):
- Canary monitoring runbook with alert thresholds and on-call escalation path.
- Rollback playbook (automated rollback steps + manual approval path).

Open trade-offs and decisions to document:
- Mode consolidation vs. separate endpoints: chose single /v1/infer to reduce surface but increases parameter multiplexing complexity.
- Streaming deferred to reduce infra risk in MVP.
- Determinism default set to false to avoid harming throughput; provide seed option for reproducibility in evals.

Links and artifacts:
- Eval bank: https://confluence.redwood.ai/evals/minimal-endpoint-bank (internal)
- Draft SDK examples: https://drive.redwood.ai/hosted-infer/sdk-minimal.zip
- Canary dashboard mock: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/minimal-infer-canary

- Finalize API schema and publish OpenAPI spec (due 2025-02-21).
- Ship initial SDK snippets for dogfood (due 2025-02-25).
- Schedule security review with Security (target 2025-02-26).
